It's better that we are alone.

Given the scale of the universe, and the vast length of time that came before life on Earth, it is very very improbable that life didn't evolve before us, and evolve past where we are. Therefor, we ask Fermi's Paradox: where's all the fucking aliens? There should be aliens, and they should be very technologically advanced, they've had 10 billion years and a billion trillion trillion planets to do it.

So what happened? There's a few theories. Plague is one, wiped them all out. Another is that they're choosing not to contact us, like we're zoo animals or one of those backwards Amazonian tribes on display. Another is that our planet is remote, and unreachable, which means we'll never reach them. None of these situations are good.

So, due to the fact that we've had zero contact from those that came before us for any number of reasons all of which are bad, it's better if we're alone. Just a statistical anomaly in an otherwise barren universe.

Edit: There are other proposed answers to Fermi's Paradox, which can be looked up online. They include such cheerful theories as, "Life always destroys itself" or "Someone or something is destroying intelligent life" or "Alien life is too alien for humans to even comprehend them". Again, none of the resolutions to the paradox are good.

Edit 2: My favorite answer to the Fermi Paradox? We're in a simulation. Our computers are advancing at an astonishing rate; pretty soon, we'll be able to simulate an entire universe. What says we haven't already done this, and we're in it right now? Maybe our human software designers are only interested in simulating humanity. Maybe they haven't been discovered yet. Either way, it's actually statistically probable that we're in a simulation.
